text:
anya: Quick question — can we add a tiny "scope" control in Console analytics so you can flip between global / per-route / per-model without rebuilding filters?

mike: I keep duplicating queries for the same metric across routes. A scope dropdown would save time. :100:

jess: Do you mean like a top-level selector that modifies the query context (route_id / model_id) instead of embedding those as filter clauses?

anya: yeah. UX idea: a left pill with three states (All, Route, Model). When Route/Model is selected we show a small picker and automatically scope saved views.

mike: Implementation note: backend telemetry API already accepts optional route_id/model_id in the request. We could add a new query param `scope` and synthesize filters server-side.

jess: prefer server-side because front-end currently duplicates logic for timezones / sampling. Also helps with shareable URLs: `/console/analytics?scope=route&route=abc&view=xyz` instead of encoding big JSON in the URL.

david: Two cautions: 1) our metrics rollups are at route-level only for some preaggregates — if we scope to model we might need to fall back to raw events or present approximate numbers. 2) quotas: per-route quota buckets exist; scoping should surface which quota the view hits.

anya: good call. UX should signal when data is approximate and which quota applies (tooltip). Also want save-as behavior: saved view can be either scope-agnostic (shares across routes) or bound to a specific route/model.

mike: How about a checkbox in the save modal: "Bind to current scope" (checked = include route/model in the saved query). Default unchecked.

jess: For programmatic access: we should extend the saved-views API to accept `scope: ["global"|"route"|"model"]` and optional `scope_id`. Then Console can call the API consistently.

anya: Can the console export a permalink that other teams can open with the same scope applied?

jess: yes — permalink pattern: `/analytics/view/{view_id}?scope=route&route_id=...` or if saved view is bound it could be `/analytics/view/{view_id}` and server resolves scope from view metadata.

mike: Quick prod concern: many existing saved views are implicitly route-specific (people copy queries per-route). If we make default unchecked we won't break current behavior. But we should run a migration to detect views that include `route_id` and mark them as bound.

david: Also add telemetry: event `analytics.view.open` with properties `{view_id, scope, scope_id, user_type}` so we can measure adoption and errors.

anya: Action items:
- jess: draft API PR for saved-views changes and permalink behavior.
- mike: add scope dropdown UI mock + save modal checkbox.
- david: define telemetry events and quota signal UX copy.
- anya: write short RFC describing migration plan and messaging to power users.

console-bot: deploy-checklist: create feature-flag `analytics_scope_picker` behind rollout.

mike: timeline: I can spike UI next week, jess can probably get API proto in 5 days.

anya: Sounds good. I'll put these in the product board and tag owners. If anything else pops up, ping me. :thumbsup:
